title: Adaptive traffic hedging with warm-cache preservation and cost-priority region spillover
creator: Lena Schwartz
description: Build an adaptive traffic hedging layer for model variant rollouts that preserves warmed KV/prefix caches, routes by cost-tier and latency SLOs, and performs prioritized region spillover when capacity or compatibility constraints appear. The goal is to reduce cold-cache regressions during canaries and A/B tests while ensuring predictable cost and graceful regional failovers.
background: We see repeated issues during canary rollouts where traffic shifted to a new variant causes cold KV cache misses and large latency spikes. Manual rollbacks happen too late. Existing routing only supports simple weighted splits and proximity-based region fallback; we need a compact runtime-level hedging strategy that accounts for cache state, tenant affinity, and capacity tiers.
proposed_solution: Implement a routing middleware that: 1) maintains per-variant cache-warmness scores using lightweight probes and recent-KV-hit metrics; 2) applies hedged requests for a configurable fraction of canary traffic to both control and variant (fast hedging) when warmness is low; 3) preferentially route overflow to lower-cost capacity tiers (burst/dedicated) only after compatibility and latency checks; 4) when region capacity is constrained, perform cost-prioritized spillover with an eviction policy that preserves hot-tenant affinity; 5) integrate an auto-rollback signal that triggers when hedged latency delta and error rate exceed thresholds for X minutes.
rollout_plan: Phase 1: feature-flag gated service behind runtime config; internal alpha to staging with synthetic workloads (2 weeks). Phase 2: enable for 10% of small-tenant canaries with canary probes and traffic-hedge fraction=20% (1 week). Phase 3: ramp to 50% across low-latency tenants with dashboards and automated rollback enabled (2 weeks). Phase 4: enable cost-priority region spillover and run cross-region soak tests (1 week).
acceptance_criteria: 1) Hedged canary traffic reduces cold-start tail latency by >= 30% compared to baseline for the same variant. 2) KV/warmness score correlates with observed latency (pearson r > 0.6). 3) Auto-rollback triggers within configured window when latency delta > 200ms and error rate + p95 token latency breach both occur. 4) Region spillover honors cost-tier preferences and never routes more than configured extra capacity per tier. 5) Verified with synthetic workload and two real customer canaries in staging with no customer-facing errors.
testing_plan: - Unit tests for warmness scoring and hedging decision logic. - Integration test: spin up control+variant with programmable cold caches and verify hedged requests hit both variants. - Chaos test: simulate regional capacity loss and validate spillover and rollback. - Load test: replicate 5k req/s with mixed sequence lengths and confirm SLOs. - Post-deploy canary run for two internal services for 48 hours.
monitoring_and_alerting: Dashboards: hedged_vs_unhedged_latency, variant_warmness_heatmap, spillover_volume_by_region, rollback_trigger_count. Alerts: auto-rollback fired, hedged-latency-delta > threshold (P0), unexpected increase in spillover cost (> 30% over baseline).
